# Devkit

Tools for working on markup.nvim: the inspector, the stress test and the playground.

Source: `lua/markup/devkit/init.lua`

```lua
function markup.devkit.inspect()
```

Toggles the inspector for the view in the current window or tab.

## markup.devkit.tree

Source: `lua/markup/devkit/tree.lua`

Fields:

- `fps_steps`: `table` - Steps of the frame rate slider, the last one for no cap at all.
- `offsets`: `table<integer, integer>` - first child shown per parent
- `options`: `{ key: string, label: string, desc: string, shortcut: string, default: boolean }[]` - What the options popup lists, in order.
- `samples`: `{ at: number, ms: number }[]` - the last frames of the target, oldest first
- `stamps`: `table` - When each frame of the last second came, oldest at `first`. Separate from `samples`, which only keeps enough frames for the sparkline.
- `timer`: `unknown` - Frames per second fall back to zero once the target goes quiet, which no commit would ever tell.
